significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a form-(ii) causal decomposition—distinct features for when a proposition is "attributed as believed" versus "asserted as fact" can independently control the corresponding behaviors—and a form-(iii) predictive coupling in which feature "entanglement ... predicts behavioral conflation on epistemic benchmarks." This would fix expectations across models and tuning stages and provide a mechanism for the behavioral distinction discussed in “Language models cannot reliably distinguish belief from knowledge and fact,” rather than merely showing that epistemic information is decodable; it is therefore more constraining than the usual SAE feature-plus-steering claim exemplified by work such as Templeton et al. (2024). Verified false would rule against a clean dictionary-level decomposition, although SAE failure or feature splitting would limit how strongly it rules out separable representations generally; true and false are nonetheless distinguishable, and after substituting the generic LLM-beliefs topic, the causal independence and entanglement–error relation disappear, so the score is not inherited from the topic.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: a targeted intervention, "steering the responsible features," and an "entanglement metric" relating feature overlap to behavioral belief/fact conflation. The steering handle is mainly post hoc and must be rediscovered per model, but the entanglement metric is potentially ex ante because it is asserted to predict benchmark conflation after features are re-extracted, leaving an action window for researchers or model auditors before deployment. Scope extends across "model sizes and instruction-tuning stages" but not clearly across architectures or modalities, and the downstream users are primarily interpretability researchers and epistemic-behavior auditors; substituting the topic alone removes both the predictor and intervention, supporting reach above the topic median but not universal transfer.
